title: Sliding window
summary: Keep a contiguous summary current so the whole scan is O(n).

parts.rule: Keep a contiguous summary up to date while the window’s right edge advances and the left edge only moves forward. Aim for total linear work across the whole scan.
parts.why: Subarray and substring constraints — longest with at most k distinct, minimum covering length — look quadratic if you restart sums. A window reuses the previous summary instead of rebuilding it.
parts.example: SAMPLE: longest substring with at most two distinct characters. Expand right, update counts in a map, and while the distinct count exceeds two, advance left and decrement. Track the best width. Each index enters and leaves the window at most once.
parts.use: Use a sliding window for contiguous constraints on arrays or strings, especially with a hash map of frequencies or a running sum. Prefer a deque window when you need the window’s minimum or maximum in amortized constant time.
parts.refuse: Refuse a window when the needed subset is not contiguous. Refuse shrinking the left edge backward. Refuse resetting the whole summary on every move when an incremental update exists.

body:
Rule. Keep a contiguous summary up to date while the window’s right edge advances and the left edge only moves forward. Aim for total linear work across the whole scan.

Why it matters. Subarray and substring constraints — longest with at most k distinct, minimum covering length — look quadratic if you restart sums. A window reuses the previous summary instead of rebuilding it.

SAMPLE example. SAMPLE: longest substring with at most two distinct characters. Expand right, update counts in a map, and while the distinct count exceeds two, advance left and decrement. Track the best width. Each index enters and leaves the window at most once.

When to use. Use a sliding window for contiguous constraints on arrays or strings, especially with a hash map of frequencies or a running sum. Prefer a deque window when you need the window’s minimum or maximum in amortized constant time.

When to refuse. Refuse a window when the needed subset is not contiguous. Refuse shrinking the left edge backward. Refuse resetting the whole summary on every move when an incremental update exists.
